To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) statistical forecasting support improves the accuracy of forecasts, not because it reduces the biases, but because it reduces the random error, (ii) the performance improvement does not depend on whether forecasts are based on cleansed time series and (iii) optimal forecasts that take promotional perturbations into full account further improve the accuracy.
(a) statistical forecasts that do not consider promotional effects are more useful than unaided forecasts, but (b) forecasts that consider promotional effects are even more accurate.

(1) the use of statistical forecasts can reduce the random error in the forecast without affecting the biases in the unaided forecasts, and (2) the use of optimal statistical forecasts can eliminate the biases in the forecast and reduce the random error.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people make forecasts and the conditions under which they do so.
the effectiveness of different forecasting support systems.

the effects of sporadic perturbative events on forecasting accuracy and with the effectiveness of different forecasting support systems in reducing the effects of these perturbations on the accuracy of forecasts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
statistical forecasts are useful, but the more detailed statement would be that they are useful if they are based on series that take promotional effects (and other sporadic effects) into account.
the more effort that is invested, the more accurate the forecasts will be.
the more effort is put into producing forecasts, the more accurate these forecasts are.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effectiveness of forecasting support depends on the extent of sporadic perturbative effects and that the effectiveness of different approaches to forecasting support depends on their ability to reduce these effects.
the use of statistical forecasts can be beneficial even when the data are subject to sporadic disturbances.
the effectiveness of forecasting support depends on the extent to which the series is subject to perturbations and on the type of support provided.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effectiveness of different forecasting approaches depends on the proportion of time series periods that contain promotions.
the accuracy of forecasts can be improved by providing support that is tailored to the type of series being forecasted.

companies should not assume that forecasters will be able to forecast effectively without the support of statistical forecasts, especially in cases where the series are subject to sporadic, unpredictable perturbations.
